title: CORRECTION-REKEY-01 — trust-anchor rotation 2026-10-24 (argus-lab-2026q4 → argus-lab-2026q4r2): originals preserved, original signatures verifiable, rotation recorded in-chain

subject.trigger: external audit of public materials (2026-11-13/14, ARG-01): the 2026-10-24 key rotation was recorded only in a commit message (65e6149d), violating the registry's own key-rotation policy ('new key gets a new key_id and a chain-linked amendment')

changes.from: argus-lab-2026q4 — private key lost in a lab environment reset on 2026-10-24 (private key never committed, never exposed; public key SHA-256 0c69ada603cc753d31531e8b64910cf6edf1cf6de5a159bf7369141495e36072)
changes.to: argus-lab-2026q4r2 — all records #0000–#0021 are signed under it; the old public key is restored to keys/argus-lab-2026q4.pub.json
changes.rationale: Rotation was forced by private-key loss, not by compromise. Restoring the old public key keeps the original signatures verifiable without git archaeology; the verifier now resolves each record's key by signer_key_id (fail-closed).

changes.from: originally signed under argus-lab-2026q4; originals preserved verbatim at attestations/evidence/rekey-2026-10-24/*.pre-rekey.json (SHA-256 pinned in evidence below)
changes.to: re-signed under argus-lab-2026q4r2 with content preserved — the only content difference across the whole re-sign is the structurally forced prev_record_hash rebind in #0001 (old chain head da9ce991a7d63032199a443630b848465e8042a42722a43117f91274c60a49bc); re-sign commit 65e6149d
changes.rationale: Verified 2026-11-14 with the repo's own primitives (canonical/verifyPayload under loadPublicKeyById('argus-lab-2026q4')): both original signatures are VALID under the restored public key, and #0000's content is byte-identical pre/post re-sign. The old chain is reconstructible end-to-end from the preserved files.

changes.from: key-rotation policy required a chain-linked amendment; the 2026-10-24 rotation lived only in a commit message
changes.to: rotation recorded in-chain by this correction; attestations/README.md now states the lost-key procedure explicitly (publish old public key, re-sign with content preserved, chain-linked correction with the old key's SHA-256 pinned)
changes.rationale: The event most in need of a seal was itself unsigned — the audit's point. This record is the fix.

status.applied_to: tools/registry (multi-key verifier), keys/argus-lab-2026q4.pub.json restored, attestations/evidence/rekey-2026-10-24/ preserved, attestations/README.md lost-key procedure added

notes: External audit (2026-11-13/14) flagged ARG-01: the 2026-10-24 trust-anchor rotation was the registry event most needing a seal, yet was itself only a commit message. Nothing is rewritten: sealed record JSONs stay untouched (immutability rule); this correction records the custody event. Scope of re-signing was exactly #0000–#0001 (the only records that existed pre-rotation); #0002 onwards were born under r2. Human-readable mirror: site/public/dossiers/registry.md after the next build-index.
